C9000285.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 285 (Counterexamples to Baum–Connes and Kadison–Kaplansky.; papers: A torsion-free counterexample to reduced Baum–Connes injectivity; A torsion-free counterexample to the Kadison–Kaplansky projection conjecture; An irrational-trace counterexample to reduced Baum–Connes; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

PUBLISHABLE_REVIEW.statement: A genuinely publishable mathematical result, with verified novelty if claimed, passes the Host's independent Reviewer; overlap verification alone does not certify the campaign or any main theorem.

MAIN_IRR.statement: There exist a finitely generated group G and a scalar projection b in C_r^*(G) with irrational canonical trace, whose K0 class is outside coefficient-free proper reduced assembly.

MAIN_KK.statement: There exists a finitely generated torsion-free group with a scalar reduced-algebra projection of canonical trace strictly between zero and one half.

MAIN_INJ.statement: There exists a finitely generated torsion-free group containing an embedded torus with integral orientation detector, but with its rank-zero Bott class zero in reduced K0; the torus Dirac class has infinite order and zero reduced assembly image.

C_OVERLAP_AUDIT.statement: Resolve the exact simultaneous-overlap dependency by a universal proof or an admissible exact counterexample. The DAG currently follows the universal-proof alternative; the other route is not required as an additional obligation.

G_COUNTEREXAMPLE.statement: An exact counterexample to a named overlap-chain assertion satisfies all applicable graphical hypotheses, and proves lexicographic minimality if it uses a minimal-diagram assertion.

G_DISTINCT.statement: Under the exact geometry hypotheses, different indexed copies do not share a simple path of length at least lambda times either source girth, and different indices give different subgraphs.

G_DIAGRAM_EXIST.statement: Every inflated coned loop admits a finite connected plane multigraph diagram with the prescribed exterior side occurrences and bounded contours assigned to translated relator copies; lexicographic minimizers in faces and then edges exist.

G_SURGERY.statement: The minimal-diagram face omission, equal-copy mergers, unmarked-leaf deletion, bounded-face bridge deletion, and inverse-pair folding preserve the applicable side data and assignments and improve the claimed lexicographic complexity.

G_ARCS.statement: In every lexicographically minimal adjustable-side diagram, bounded faces have perimeter at least their assigned girth; every incident compressed arc is shorter than lambda times that girth, and generator-side arcs have unit length.

G_EULER.statement: For a compressed minimal diagram with m prescribed sides, b arcs and F bounded faces, Euler and valence counting give v-b+F=1, 2b>=3(v-m), and F/lambda<=2b, including trees and isolated marked vertices.

G_COUNT.statement: Every such diagram satisfies (1/lambda-6)F<=6m-6 and b<=6m for 0<lambda<=1/12.

G_DESIGNATED.statement: For an avoiding path closed by one designated P side, no arc has both exterior incidences in that same linear side occurrence; the bridge excursion deletion respects marked positions even when marked vertices are revisited.

G_AVOID.statement: If a coned edge path of length L joins x,a in P and avoids c_P, then d_P(x,a)<=12(L+1)lambda*sigma(P).

G_FILL.statement: Every coned edge loop of length n>0 has a filling using at most 12n closed relations of perimeter at most four, with constants independent of the graphs, alphabet and lambda.

G_COARSE.statement: A simply connected 2-complex with 2-cell attaching lengths at most M and linear combinatorial isoperimetric constant C has delta-hyperbolic 1-skeleton, with delta depending only on M and C and with no local-finiteness or bounded-valence assumption.

G_THIN.statement: There exists an integer D0 independent of lambda, the graphs and the alphabet such that every vertex of a geodesic triangle in the coned graph is within D0 of a vertex on another side.

G_ROOT.statement: In the coned graph, assuming vertex D0-thinness, fix A=c_P!=R and one A-to-R geodesic with first group vertex a. If Q!=P, x in P intersect Q and d(c_Q,R)<=d(A,R), an A-avoiding walk from x to a has length at most L0=4D0+8, including equal-distance centers and either allowed root type.

G_OVERLAP.statement: With universal D0, t=D0+3 and L0=4D0+8, every intersection of P with a different Q whose center is no farther from the root than c_P lies in the same intrinsic induced P-ball about the first vertex a of one fixed root geodesic, of radius floor(12(L0+1)lambda*sigma(P)).

G_ALGEBRA.statement: The source-bound rational LP has exact minimum min(4m-b)=6, and the saved affine and root-constant certificates prove the stated numerical implications for every admissible value of their premises; this assertion does not certify the topological premises.

G_SHARP_COUNT.statement: Under all original geometry hypotheses, every nontrivial minimal adjustable-side diagram has b<=4m-6 and (1/lambda-6)F<=4m-6; the isolated case has F=b=0 and is handled separately.

G_SHARP_AVOID.statement: Under all original geometry hypotheses, every c_P-avoiding coned edge path of length L>=1 with endpoints x,a in P satisfies d_P(x,a)<=(4L-2)lambda*sigma(P); for L=0 the distance is zero.

G_SHARP_FILL.statement: Under all original geometry hypotheses, every coned edge loop of length n>0 is a product of at most 8n conjugates of closed edge relations of perimeter at most four, giving the corresponding combinatorial disk area bound even with singular intermediate contours.

G_SHARP_OVERLAP.statement: Under all original geometry hypotheses there is a universal integer vertex-thinness constant D0 independent of lambda. For every allowed root R!=c_P and one fixed c_P-to-R geodesic with first group vertex a, all P intersect Q with Q!=P and d(c_Q,R)<=d(c_P,R) lie in the same intrinsic induced P-ball about a of radius floor((16D0+30)lambda*sigma(P)).

IRR_DATA.statement: The labelled expander and parameter choices in data.tex:prop:data exist, including isometric embeddings, uniform expansion, sufficiently small induced tree balls, and diverging code-dimension gaps.

IRR_CYCLES.statement: The ordinary finite-support cycle space of X over F2 is the internal algebraic direct sum of the cycle spaces of all indexed copies.

IRR_CODES.statement: The finite-field codes with prescribed words, dimensions and primal/dual distance used in module.tex exist.

IRR_MODULE.statement: The globally generated relation module W0 has W0 intersect F_p^P equal to C_P perpendicular for every copy P.

IRR_MARGINALS.statement: The compact-dual restriction to each copy is exactly the prescribed code and has uniform Haar marginal, with prescribed-word probability p^(-k_i).

IRR_VALID.statement: The enabled-graph construction makes designated valid copies pairwise disjoint isolated expander components and gives the asserted local deficits elsewhere.

IRR_GLOBAL_DEFICIT.statement: For every enabled remaining graph and every finite vertex set Y, d|Y|-2|E(Y)| >= (c/2)|Y|, including the projected-cycle localization and disjoint cycle-rank charges.

IRR_REP.statement: The Fourier/crossed-product realization identifies the asserted fiber operators with a faithful reduced representation and gives the canonical trace integral.

IRR_GAP.statement: The self-adjoint enabled-graph operator has the asserted kernel and the uniform gap min(rho,c^2/(8d)) on its complement in all relevant reduced fibers.

IRR_PROJECTION.statement: Continuous functional calculus of the uniformly gapped reduced operator gives the actual scalar projection b0 in C_r^*(V semidirect Gamma), with the asserted fiber diagonals.

IRR_TRACE.statement: The projection has trace sum_i p^(-k_i), which is irrational by the non-eventually-periodic base-p expansion.

IRR_TRACE_IMAGE.statement: For every countable discrete group, the canonical trace on every integral degree-zero coefficient-free proper reduced assembly class is rational, with the exact assembly comparison used by the manuscript.

KK_GEOMETRY.statement: The tower, path-recovery labelling, pruning and nilpotent voltage covers give the claimed embedded copies, common-root domains, forest complement and torsion-free finitely generated group.

KK_SAMPLING.statement: Finite voltage and matrix-weight sampling simultaneously enforce the girth conditions and full regular-norm approximation to the nilpotent fiber model.

KK_BAND.statement: The local upper band survives removal of overlaps and the unused forest edges to give a uniformly separated, nonempty global reduced matrix spectral band.

KK_SMALL_TRACE.statement: The global upper spectral projection has strictly positive unnormalized matrix trace less than one half, including the weighted losses from all indexed copies.

KK_SCALAR.statement: The quantitative reduced free-product compression converts the small matrix projection to a scalar projection of the same trace while preserving torsion-freeness and finite generation.

INJ_GEOMETRY.statement: The layered labelling, sequential expansion, pruning, Heisenberg voltage cover and common-root domains produce the claimed torsion-free finitely generated group with embedded torus.

INJ_DETECTOR.statement: An integral degree-two class restricts to the oriented torus generator and detects the torus Dirac K-homology class as infinite order.

INJ_BOTT_MODEL.statement: The localized rank-zero Bott families are bounded operators and admit the required even/odd and odd/positive-even norm-continuous homotopies.

INJ_REDUCED_NORM.statement: The finite sampled group-algebra operators and homotopies approximate the Bott model in the asserted reduced regular norm quotient.

INJ_FINITE_TRANSFER.statement: The cancellation in the norm quotient yields an actual finite witness to vanishing of the embedded torus Bott class in one reduced group algebra.

INJ_ASSEMBLY.statement: The compact-support K-homology conventions, torus Dirac/Bott identification and reduced assembly naturality give an infinite-order assembly kernel class from the detector and analytic vanishing.
